result.note: Tests the June 2026 tax waiver for foreign portfolio investors in government securities and its rupee-defence aim.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about a tax measure announced by the Finance Ministry in June 2026:
items: It waived income and capital gains taxes for foreign portfolio investors in government securities.
It aimed to draw debt capital to support the rupee after equity outflows of USD 27.6 billion in 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. On 8 June 2026 the Finance Ministry exempted foreign portfolio investors in government securities from income and capital gains taxes. The aim was to defend a sliding rupee by attracting debt capital, seen as stickier than the equity money that had flowed out.
questions.source: The Finance Ministry waived income and capital gains taxes for foreign portfolio investors in government securities, aiming to defend a sliding rupee after USD 27.6 billion in equity outflows this year by drawing in stickier debt capital.
